title: Inspecting Drain Pipe Slope for Long-Term Maintenance
description: Maintaining accurate pipe pitch along horizontal drainage lines is essential for reliable self-scouring flow. Insufficient slope causes wastewater to move too slowly, allowing heavy solids and grease to settle at the bottom of the pipe over time. Conversely, excessive slope can allow liquids to drain rapidly while leaving solid debris behind. Routine maintenance inspections should evaluate pipe hangers and structural supports to identify sagged sections, commonly known as pipe bellies, where standing water collects. Verifying pitch and securing loose supports prevents recurring blockages and maintains continuous gravity flow.

Inspecting Drain Pipe Slope for Long-Term Maintenance

Maintaining accurate pipe pitch along horizontal drainage lines is essential for reliable self-scouring flow. Insufficient slope causes wastewater to move too slowly, allowing heavy solids and grease to settle at the bottom of the pipe over time. Conversely, excessive slope can allow liquids to drain rapidly while leaving solid debris behind. Routine maintenance inspections should evaluate pipe hangers and structural supports to identify sagged sections, commonly known as pipe bellies, where standing water collects. Verifying pitch and securing loose supports prevents recurring blockages and maintains continuous gravity flow.
